title: Elastic Token Envelope — runtime-aware tranche bundler and pad decimation
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Implement an "elastic envelope" micro-batching strategy that groups requests into runtime-aware tranches and aggressively reduces pad tokens while preserving model output quality and SLOs. The feature combines three levers: 1) tranche bundling (soft grouped buckets that allow limited variance), 2) pad decimation (runtime per-batch pad budget and tail-trim heuristics), and 3) kernel affinity hints (prefer kernels tuned for longer effective sequences and sparse attention when applicable).

Background: Current static bucketing leaves substantial pad waste for mixed workloads (chat + short completion bursts). Prior work (various seqlen bucketing tickets) improved packing but is brittle to heavy-tail distributions and creates scheduling thrash when prefill and decode phases interleave. The Elastic Token Envelope aims to reduce this friction by letting the scheduler form variable-width envelopes that trade a small latency tail for larger pad savings and throughput gains.

Key design points: 
- Envelope definition: each envelope has (min_len, soft_cap, hard_cap, pad_budget). Requests up to soft_cap are eligible for fast-path kernels; those between soft_cap and hard_cap are allowed with a per-envelope pad_budget used to fill to the next kernel-favorable boundary.
- Tranche bundler: runtime heuristics build tranches from recent seqlen histograms + token arrival time. Uses exponential decay to weight recent bursts. Tranches are closed when pad_budget or time_budget is reached.
- Tail-trim pad decimation: for prefill-heavy requests we apply a probabilistic tail-trim that removes trailing pad tokens up to a budget while keeping token alignment for KV caching. This reduces per-token compute for decode-heavy workloads.
- Kernel affinity hints: envelopes emit kernel_hints (e.g., "long-seq-optimized", "sparse-attn-enabled") to the kernel selector. Kernel selector maps hints to kernel variants (cuBLAS fused kernels, custom sparse kernels) when available; fallback to default if unavailable.
- Prefill/decode scheduling interactions: prefill requests are prioritized for forming envelopes when doing so enables subsequent cache reuse and therefore reduces duplicate compute. Decode requests may be kicked to a fast-path if latency-critical and within envelope soft_cap.

Acceptance criteria / success metrics: 
- Pad token reduction: >= 30% reduction in pad tokens per second on mixed seqlen synthetic workload (long tail) relative to baseline runtime-1.19 config.
- Throughput: >= 15% increase in effective tokens/sec for the same GPU pool under same load.
- Latency: p95 decode latency should not regress by more than 10% for latency-sensitive routes; p50 should improve for batched workloads.
- Quality/regressions: zero functional regressions on our suite of 200 prompt tests (no deterministic changes), and BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-similarity within baseline thresholds for open-model comparisons.

Implementation plan: 
1) Prototype tranche bundler in runtime scheduler (Rust): implement envelope builder, pad_budget logic, and kernel_hints emission. Link: https://drive.redwood.ai/docs/elastic-envelope-proposal (design doc).
2) Integrate pad-decimation logic in prefill pipeline and ensure KV cache alignment.
3) Add kernel hint plumbing to compilation/kernels module and map to existing kernel variants.
4) Unit + integration tests: deterministic seqlen generators, KV cache correctness tests, and perf harness.
5) Staging perf runs: synthetic distributions (uniform, heavy-tail, bimodal) and replayed production traces from last 7 days.
6) Canary rollout: 5% traffic -> 25% -> 50% with rollback gates (pad token delta, cost delta, p95 latency).

Compatibility & fallbacks: feature behind runtime flag packer.mode=elastic-envelope and runtime config envelope_enabled=true. For Dedicated/Private deployments we expose a conservative default (smaller soft_cap) and an opt-in aggressive profile. If kernel_hint cannot be satisfied, scheduler falls back to legacy bucketer without dropping requests.

Observability: add metrics: envelope_count, avg_pad_tokens_per_envelope, pad_tokens_saved, kernel_hint_misses, tranche_close_reasons (time_budget|pad_budget|hard_cap), pct_prefill_in_envelope. Dashboards: runtime-1.20 -> performance/runtime/envelope.

Security & privacy: No user data leaves runtime; no new telemetry beyond aggregate metrics. Confirmed no secrets.

Rollout plan and monitoring gates:
- Canary 5% for 24h with close monitoring on pad_tokens_saved and latency p95; automatic rollback if pad savings < 10% or p95 regresses > 15% vs baseline.
- 25% for 48h with synthetic and production trace replays.
- Full rollout if all gates pass for 72h.

Related artifacts and links: 
- Design doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/docs/elastic-envelope-proposal
- Perf harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4820
- Scheduler prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/compare/elastic-envelope-proto

Notes: This ticket intentionally scopes to runtime-side scheduler and kernel hinting only. Separate follow-ups will: integrate with console autoscaling policies, add API-level traffic controls, and explore model-specific quantization-aware envelope presets.
